package_info.package_versions: All versions of the rogue app as distributed
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is malicious because it impersonates a legitimate brand to deceive users, steal credentials, deploy malware, abuse in-app purchases, and/or exfiltrate sensitive data, resulting in financial loss and reputational damage.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code presents a fake login screen, collects user credentials, and sends them to an attacker-controlled server, enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app collects sensitive credentials and transmits them to an unauthorized external server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should authenticate users with the real service backend, not exfiltrate credentials to unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may collect credentials for authentication, but only transmit them to trusted, official endpoints.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or hardcoded attacker server URLs

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after free trial period or in-app purchase event)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initiates a high-fee subscription after a free trial and hides subscription management options, resulting in unauthorized or deceptive billing.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app charges excessive fees and makes it difficult for users to cancel, exploiting legitimate billing APIs for fraud.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should clearly disclose fees and provide easy subscription management.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Subscription management is legitimate, but hiding controls and charging exorbitant fees is not.
key_indicators: Automatic billing after free trial without clear consent

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user interaction with pop-up or ad)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code displays a pop-up prompting the user to install additional software, which downloads and installs malware onto the device.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app entices users to install additional APKs, which is a common malware delivery vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should not prompt users to install unrelated or unsigned APKs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: App updates or plugins may be delivered, but only from official sources and with user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time or first launch, the app requests excessive permissions such as access to contacts, photos, and social media accounts, enabling data exfiltration and privilege escalation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app requests broad permissions unrelated to its stated functionality, increasing risk of data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should request only the permissions necessary for their core features.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some apps legitimately need access to contacts or storage, but only with clear user benefit and consent.
key_indicators: Requests for sensitive permissions without clear justification
Permission requests at install-time for unrelated features
No in-app explanation for permission use

attack_chain.action: User discovers and installs the rogue app from an app store or APK site.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is installed and can execute malicious behaviors.

attack_chain.action: App requests excessive permissions during installation or first launch.
attack_chain.leads_to: App gains access to sensitive data and device features.

attack_chain.action: App presents a fake login screen to harvest user credentials.
App initiates hidden or exorbitant in-app purchases after a free trial.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is charged excessive fees without clear consent.

attack_chain.action: App displays pop-ups or ads prompting user to install additional malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device is further compromised with additional malware.

behavioral_signatures: App requests permissions unrelated to its stated functionality
Credentials sent to non-official or hardcoded external servers
Initiation of in-app purchases with hidden or excessive fees
Pop-ups prompting installation of additional APKs or software
file_indicators: AndroidManifest.xml with excessive or unrelated permissions
Presence of hardcoded URLs/domains not associated with the legitimate brand
Obfuscated or missing subscription management UI elements
network_indicators: Outbound connections to non-brand, attacker-controlled domains
Downloads of APKs from non-official sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor app stores and APK sites for apps using your brand name or assets. Analyze app permissions for excessive or unrelated requests. Inspect network traffic for credential exfiltration or connections to suspicious domains. Review in-app purchase flows for hidden or excessive fees. Use behavioral analysis to detect pop-ups prompting installation of additional software. Employ static and dynamic analysis tools to identify hardcoded attacker infrastructure and obfuscated code.
